rationale: The CADASIL trial used a stripped soybean-oil comparator. Mixed and animal studies supply no isolated refined soybean-oil estimate for Parkinson walking slowness.
The available almond-oil studies use external exposure, bundles or animal models. Cold-press grade and an isolated dietary effect on Parkinson depressive symptoms remain unmeasured.

The Parkinson cohort analyses overlap and do not report a numerical item-level postural-instability estimate or the oil processing grade needed for attribution. The baseline item tile remains a traceable follow-up.

Completed NCT07047105 has no posted fatigue data. NCT07752329 is not yet recruiting and shows no results. Both study a related Zanthoxylum armatum extract. The existing Maybe True anchor of 50.005 remains.
Diagnostic and risk review evidence, a daily-living composite and caffeine testing supply no brewed-green-tea handwriting estimate for Parkinson disease.
Carvone inhalation and animal extract studies measure alertness, exploration or feeding rather than an isolated toasted-caraway Parkinson apathy comparison.

NCT05084365 has unposted Parkinson cognition outcomes for sulforaphane, and recruiting NCT07334366 targets attention or vigilance with broccoli-sprout extract. Neither yet supplies results or exact raw-broccoli fit.

The carrot food-frequency entry lacks a hallucination outcome, and the poisoning case attributes symptoms to contamination rather than raw carrot. The reviewed literature supplies no raw-carrot Parkinson visual-hallucination comparison.
The completed ALTIS dialysis study registers a mixed lentil-flour supplement for muscle mass. It gives no canned-lentil exposure or Parkinson walking endpoint.
The focused PubMed match is a fecal microbiota transplant safety study. Animal basil studies and laboratory apparatus references do not provide dietary basil OFF time.
Bundled diets, constituent studies and two Zucchini surname collisions supply no isolated grilled-zucchini executive-function assessment in Parkinson disease.
Completed NCT07630571 gives an oral-pain endpoint and a grapeseed-oil control with another component. Results and a cold-press specification remain unavailable.
The household manuscript analysis documents historical dietetic classifications of parsley. Mixed diets and human experimental kinetics supply no dried parsley and Parkinson handwriting comparison.
The rat speech-related study used corn oil as an injection carrier. Shared vehicles and communication composites supply no refined oral corn-oil speech effect in Parkinson disease.
Piperine models report composite motor outcomes without individual dystonia, and the culinary pepper chemistry source has no dystonia comparison.

The 1980 printed index resolves to the previously assessed Johns report of intact bay leaves lodged after meals. A separate ground-leaf metabolism trial did not measure swallowing. The mechanically intact leaves do not establish a Parkinson ground-bay-leaf effect.
Caraway company and cited-name matches provide no exposure. Isolated carvone or multicomponent extracts did not measure toasted-caraway effects on Parkinson dystonia.
The precursor review notes green beans as a composition source. Existing mixture and animal studies do not isolate cooked green beans for Parkinson executive function.
The two multicomponent cookie registrations list gait speed and report no fall counts. The delivery-formulation review does not measure cold-pressed grapeseed oil and falls in Parkinson disease.
Injected sunflower oil was a shared model vehicle. The dietary association reports overall burden, with no cold-pressed sunflower-oil Parkinson olfaction estimate.

The original depression comparison DOI 10.18311/jnr/2021/27128 gives a tulsi–cardamom mixture and a green-tea comparator. Allocation, formulation, quantitative outcome tables and an attributable between-arm effect remain open.
Ginger appears in diagnostic odor tests and multiodor training, including the SCENT post-COVID protocol. The checked reports do not isolate grated dietary ginger for Parkinson olfactory impairment.
Parsley is a manganese source in the review and part of a Parkinson menu. The relevant records give no isolated dried parsley and dyskinesia comparison.
Cinnamon-labeled smell tests and a multi-herb case do not isolate culinary cinnamon for Parkinson dream enactment.
